events.description: The Pierson Library Open Mic is now accepting songwriters, comedians, poets, guitar strummers, saxophone wailers, sleight-of-handers, jugglers, fire breathers (be safe, though!), drag queens, drag kings, afab queens, contortionists, mesmerists, psychics, short-story tellers, theremin wobblers, aerialists, ballerinas (and ballerinos), cowboys, boxers, hula-hoop wigglers, lion tamers, geek acts, burlesque acts, card counters, orators, clowns, mimes, and tuba blowers; maybe a couple other things as well. events.title: Engage: The Human Dimension of a Practicing Philosophy
events.description: Join the Pierson Library and Shelburne neighbor Nick Marconi in a new bi-monthly journey into philosophy. The word philosophy comes from the Greek philos, which means the love in friendship, and Sophia (wisdom), hence philosophia, a movement toward the wisdom and mutual understanding of friends. For this practice we will engage one another in what it means to be human. Each session will be different, and it is not necessary to attend every session. To register, please call the library at [contact omitted].

events.title: Monday Morning Book Club: The Frozen River
events.description: Join us for a discussion of The Frozen River by Ariel Lawhon, a gripping historical mystery inspired by the real life of 18th-century midwife Martha Ballard. Set in Maine in 1789, the novel begins when a man is discovered frozen in the Kennebec River and Martha is called upon to determine the cause of death. A respected healer and keen observer of her community, Martha keeps a detailed diary that soon entangles her in a web of secrets, accusations, and injustice—particularly when her findings contradict those of a powerful local physician. As suspicion deepens and a trial approaches, Martha pursues the truth despite growing personal risk. Richly researched and vividly told, the novel brings to life a courageous woman who defied social conventions to seek justice in a world determined to silence her. Copies are available at the first-floor circulation desk. New members are always welcome!

events.title: Music & Movement with Stephen Coronella

events.title: Tech Help Tuesday
events.description: Have a tech problem you just can’t figure out? Have an app that’s giving you trouble? Does your smartphone leave you flummoxed? We can help. Book a 30-minute appointment with one of our tech-savvy librarians who can help you tame that tech problem! To register, please call the library at [contact omitted].

events.title: Tuesday Night Book Club: The Wind in the Willows
events.description: Join us for a discussion of The Wind in the Willows by Kenneth Grahame, a beloved classic that celebrates friendship, home, and the quiet pleasures of the natural world. Set along the idyllic English riverbank, the story follows the gentle Mole as he befriends the adventurous Water Rat and becomes part of a close-knit circle that includes the wise Badger and the impulsive, ever-troublesome Toad. From peaceful river picnics to daring escapades and the reclaiming of Toad Hall, the friends navigate changing seasons and unexpected challenges together. Lyrical, humorous, and timeless, the novel offers a warm reflection on loyalty, belonging, and the comforts of home. Copies are available at the first-floor circulation desk. New members are always welcome!

events.title: Noontime Poetry Reading Society
events.description: This group is for poetry readers, poetry writers, and the poetically curious alike! For the first half hour we take turns, taking the lectern and reading aloud together from whole poetry collections. Whenever we finish one, we vote on the next. We’re currently reading Women Poets from Antiquity to Now. The second half of the session is devoted to poetic reflection, news, and the sharing of poems of your own (that you’ve written, recently discovered, or old faves). There’s a take-home prompt at the end for your own poetic practice. We hope to see you there!

Monika Jaeckle has been a practitioner and teacher of alignment-based yoga for more than forty years. Please bring your own mat. To register, please call the library at [contact omitted]
